record.narrative: No assessments are due, and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so this analyze stage allocates the 12 requested analysis slots to the remaining active, untested, decision-relevant probes. These comparisons directly test whether the core dataset-internal associations and the context-sensitive PTEN-loss association persist across chromosomal-instability/ploidy strata and lineage interaction. The selected set covers: (1) MSI-high and TP53-loss effects in the high- and low-aneuploidy strata (H240, H241, H244, H245), completing the aneuploidy complement for two core predictors; (2) low-aneuploidy complements for SMARCA4-loss and KEAP1-loss (H246, H247), because their high-aneuploidy effects were already accepted; (3) PTEN-loss in TP53-intact high-aneuploidy and in triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact high- and low-aneuploidy contexts (H243, H248, H249), to determine whether PTEN evidence remains robust across instability levels in previously supported backgrounds; (4) PTEN-loss in TP53-intact/research_signature_a-positive lines separated by high versus low ploidy (H222, H242), refining the signature-dependent PTEN pattern; and (5) the PTEN-loss squamous-lineage interaction (H232), to assess whether any lineage contrast is evident after the direct TP53-intact lineage main effects remained borderline. All tests are mean-difference or interaction associations on measured variables or analysis-defined eligibility strata in the supplied dataset, not causal effects, not single-gene knockout measurements, and not external generalization claims. Results will be interpreted using signed 95% Welch intervals against the 0.15 composite dependency-score-unit threshold: accept only if the signed lower bound exceeds 0.15 in the registered direction; point estimates above threshold with lower bounds below threshold remain unresolved; sparse or borderline results will not be upgraded.

prompt:
Iteration 18/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve delivered comparisons are valid independent Welch tests with at least 20 observations in every cell. I applied the pre-specified dataset-internal threshold rule: accept only if the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction. The aneuploidy-split results strongly reinforce the core measured associations. MSI-high is associated with stronger dependency in both high-aneuploidy R216 signed 0.822, lower 0.674, upper 0.969 and low-aneuploidy R218 signed 0.762, lower 0.581, upper 0.943 strata. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency in both high-aneuploidy R217 signed 0.423, lower 0.292, upper 0.554 and low-aneuploidy R219 signed 0.425, lower 0.281, upper 0.568 strata. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency in the low-aneuploidy complement R220 signed 0.814, lower 0.718, upper 0.909, while KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency in the low-aneuploidy complement R221 signed 0.854, lower 0.763, upper 0.944. Because the high-aneuploidy SMARCA4 and KEAP1 contrasts were already accepted, the core SMARCA4/KEAP1/MSI/TP53 associations are robust across the measured chromosomal-instability split rather than confined to one side. The PTEN-loss results are more nuanced and remain context-dependent. PTEN loss is accepted in the TP53-intact/research_signature_a-positive context when separated by ploidy: high ploidy R225 signed 0.553, lower 0.380, upper 0.725 and low ploidy R226 signed 0.498, lower 0.278, upper 0.719. In the triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4 context, PTEN loss is accepted in low aneuploidy R224 signed 0.285, lower 0.164, upper 0.406, but is unresolved in high aneuploidy R223 signed 0.218, lower 0.103, upper 0.333 and unresolved among TP53-intact high-aneuploidy lines R222 signed 0.254, lower 0.128, upper 0.381. The squamous-lineage PTEN interaction R227 signed 0.069, lower -0.155, upper 0.293 is also unresolved. These are not accepted evidence of a lineage-dependent PTEN interaction or of a uniform PTEN effect across all contexts. Important caveats remain: aneuploidy/ploidy strata use analysis-defined cutpoints, several stratum tests were added after earlier exploration, and the comparisons are unadjusted marginal or subgroup contrasts, so residual confounding among measured variables cannot be ruled out. All conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or generalizable biological mechanisms. No validation is requested because the independent validation budget is exhausted.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

record.narrative:
No response deadlines or new validation results were due, and the independent validation budget is exhausted. Therefore no claim status changes are warranted from validation at this point. The evidence base in the supplied dataset is now sufficiently mature to state dataset-internal conclusions, while still avoiding causal or external-generalization language.

Bottom line: the strongest and most robust dataset-internal associations are SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger composite dependency, KEAP1 loss associated with weaker dependency, MSI-high associated with stronger dependency, and TP53 loss associated with weaker dependency. PTEN loss is not a uniform predictor; it is supported mainly in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive contexts, and its effect size remains context-dependent. Many other measured genomic, clinical, technical, and constructed marker variables do not show scientifically meaningful associations under the 0.15 composite dependency-score-unit threshold rule.

Supported findings. Using signed 95% Welch intervals and accepting only when the signed lower bound exceeds +0.15 units in the registered direction: SMARCA4 loss is repeatedly associated with stronger dependency, H5/R5 signed 0.833 lower 0.767 upper 0.898, independently validated R13 signed 0.795 lower 0.695 upper 0.896, with accepted strata including lineage, age, screen-quality, Cas9-quality, growth-rate halves, research_signature contexts, and aneuploidy strata such as H238/R214 signed 0.851 lower 0.760 upper 0.942 and H246/R220 signed 0.814 lower 0.718 upper 0.909. KEAP1 loss is repeatedly associated with weaker dependency, H7/R7 signed 0.832 lower 0.766 upper 0.897, independently validated R26 signed 0.783 lower 0.688 upper 0.878, with analogous accepted strata including H239/R215 signed 0.809 lower 0.713 upper 0.905 and H247/R221 signed 0.854 lower 0.763 upper 0.944. MSI-high is associated with stronger dependency, H41/R75 signed 0.792 lower 0.676 upper 0.907, independently validated for a TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context through H90/R87/R93 signed 0.745 lower 0.666 upper 0.825 discovery and signed 0.779 lower 0.675 upper 0.884 validation, with accepted strata across age, lineage, aneuploidy, hypoxia/EMT-related contexts, and screen-quality contexts. TP53 loss is associated overall with weaker dependency, H3/R3 signed 0.423 lower 0.327 upper 0.520, independently validated R39 signed 0.471 lower 0.334 upper 0.607, with accepted contexts including lineage main effects, low research_signature_a contexts, screen-quality strata, age-boundary strata, growth halves, and aneuploidy strata. These core claims are dataset-internal associations among measured variables or analysis-defined eligibility strata, not single-gene knockout phenotypes or causal effects.

PTEN loss is context-sensitive rather than globally uniform. It is accepted in several TP53-intact and research_signature_a-related contexts, including H58/R42 validated R53, H67/R55 validated R66, H117/R121 validated R131, and growth-half contexts such as H216/R196 and H226/R197. However, global PTEN claims are not accepted as a uniform weaker- or stronger-dependency effect, and broad lineage main effects H224/R202, H225/R203, H236/R212, and H237/R213 remain borderline or unresolved. The PTEN evidence should be interpreted as dependent on background: TP53 intact status and constructed research_signature_a positivity strengthen the apparent association, while triple-intact high-aneuploidy and some high-Cas9-quality contexts remain uncertain without signature conditioning. I registered two focused PTEN probes to test whether accepted triple-intact research_signature_a-positive PTEN evidence persists when split by aneuploidy.

Interaction findings. The most robust interaction pattern is attenuation of the TP53-loss weaker-dependency association in elevated constructed research_signature_a or research_signature_b contexts. Accepted examples include H104/R105 validated R120 for research_signature_a and H82/R77 validated R79 for research_signature_b. These should be described as context-dependent attenuation, not a new accepted opposite-direction main effect, because direct main effects in high-signature strata such as H76, H105, H157, and H158 do not support threshold-clearing opposite-direction associations. The research signatures are constructed assays without assigned biological pathways, so these interactions are data patterns in this dataset rather than mechanistic claims.

Negative or non-supported findings. Broadly, many measured predictors do not clear the scientific threshold in their registered directions: lineage subtype H1/R1, KRAS mutation H2/R2, MTAP loss H4/R4, PIK3CA mutation H6/R6, MYC amplification H8/R8, arbitrary research markers D/E/F H9-R11/R9-R11, STK11 loss H18/R32, CDKN2A loss in global and refined probes H19/R33 and related rejected CDKN2A contexts, ARID1A loss H20/R34, RB1 loss H22/R36, BRCA2 loss H39/R38, NF1 loss H40/R74, sex H42/R76, media serum H43/R52, BRAF V600E H53/R60, EGFR amplification H54/R61, ERBB2 amplification H55/R62, SMAD4 loss H56/R63, APC mutation H96/R100 and APC-Wnt interaction H97/R101, screen batch H81/R72, library main effects H23/R37 and H33/R78, matched omics coverage H35/R92, and many lineage, library, screen-quality, ploidy, MYC-expression, growth-rate, and signature interactions that did not clear the threshold. These negative findings constrain overinterpretation but are not causal nulls and do not prove absence in other datasets.

Unresolved uncertainty. The main unresolved boundaries are: PTEN broad TP53-intact lineage main effects H224/R202, H225/R203, H236/R212, and H237/R213; triple-intact high-aneuploidy PTEN without signature conditioning H248/R223; TP53-intact high-aneuploidy PTEN H243/R222; high-Cas9-quality triple-intact PTEN H146/R138; research_signature_c PTEN context H205/R185; and MSI-high within TP53-loss lines H93/R94/R106, where sparse cells produce wide intervals. Age-dependent claims are limited because age is missing for many lines. All stratum cutpoints are analysis-defined or sample-dependent, and unadjusted marginal contrasts cannot rule out confounding among correlated measured variables. Multiple exploratory subgroup tests were performed, so accepted stratum-specific effects should be weighted according to consistency, size, uncertainty, and validation, not as independent discoveries of equal strength.

Next analysis. I registered four low-multiplicity follow-up comparisons: PTEN loss within the accepted triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a-positive context split by high versus low aneuploidy, to test whether PTEN evidence holds in the high-aneuploidy side; and TP53 loss within high versus low Cas9 activity, to complete a technical-quality robustness check for the TP53 core association. If further capacity remains after these, the most valuable analysis is not broad subgroup mining but a pre-specified complete-case or high-quality robustness panel and clearer separation of PTEN contexts. No causal, single-gene, mechanistic, or external-generalization claim is supported by the current evidence.

record.narrative: With the independent validation budget exhausted and no assessments due, this explore stage focuses the remaining discovery effort on the least-settled part of the evidence base: whether PTEN-loss associations are robust technical or biological context effects rather than artifacts of sparse strata, screen quality, Cas9 quality, chromosomal-instability proxies, or constructed-signature positivity. The core associations for SMARCA4 loss (stronger dependency), KEAP1 loss (weaker dependency), MSI-high (stronger dependency), and TP53 loss (weaker dependency) are already accepted in many strata and some have independent validation, so repeating them is lower value. By contrast, PTEN loss has repeatedly accepted evidence in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds, but several broader lineage and instability contexts remain unresolved. I registered four refinements: PTEN loss in the accepted triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a-positive context with high screen ROC quality; PTEN loss in the same triple-intact context with above-median Cas9 activity; PTEN loss among TP53-intact squamous lines that are research_signature_a-positive, complementing the accepted adenocarcinoma context; and PTEN loss among TP53-intact research_signature_a-positive lines with high aneuploidy, testing whether unresolved TP53-intact high-aneuploidy PTEN evidence becomes clear once the accepted signature context is added. These are falsifiable dataset-internal comparisons, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or external generalizations. Direction convention: direction -1 claims a more negative exposed-minus-comparator composite score, i.e., stronger dependency. Results will be interpreted only if every comparison cell has at least 20 observations and signed 95% Welch lower bounds exceed the 0.15 composite-dependency-unit threshold.

prompt:
Iteration 19/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The PTEN-loss results are more nuanced and remain context-dependent. These are not accepted evidence of a lineage-dependent PTEN interaction or of a uniform PTEN effect across all contexts. Important caveats remain: aneuploidy/ploidy strata use analysis-defined cutpoints, several stratum tests were added after earlier exploration, and the comparisons are unadjusted marginal or subgroup contrasts, so residual confounding among measured variables cannot be ruled out. PTEN loss is not a uniform predictor; it is supported mainly in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive contexts, and its effect size remains context-dependent. MSI-high is associated with stronger dependency, H41/R75 signed 0.792 lower 0.676 upper 0.907, independently validated for a TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact context through H90/R87/R93 signed 0.745 lower 0.666 upper 0.825 discovery and signed 0.779 lower 0.675 upper 0.884 validation, with accepted strata across age, lineage, aneuploidy, hypoxia/EMT-related contexts, and screen-quality contexts. TP53 loss is associated overall with weaker dependency, H3/R3 signed 0.423 lower 0.327 upper 0.520, independently validated R39 signed 0.471 lower 0.334 upper 0.607, with accepted contexts including lineage main effects, low research_signature_a contexts, screen-quality strata, age-boundary strata, growth halves, and aneuploidy strata. These core claims are dataset-internal associations among measured variables or analysis-defined eligibility strata, not single-gene knockout phenotypes or causal effects.\n\nPTEN loss is context-sensitive rather than globally uniform. record.narrative: No assessments are due and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so this analyze stage does not reassess existing claims or request validation. It executes the eight active, untested, decision-relevant probes registered in the current ledger, selecting only these because they target the least-settled context-dependence of PTEN loss and the remaining technical robustness boundary for TP53 loss. H250 and H251 test PTEN loss within the already supported triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4, research_signature_a-positive background split by high versus low aneuploidy. This directly refines unresolved high-aneuploidy PTEN results and asks whether signature conditioning clarifies the effect. H252 and H253 test TP53 loss within high versus low Cas9 activity, completing a technical-quality check for the core TP53 association. H254 and H255 test PTEN loss in the triple-intact research_signature_a-positive context restricted to high screen ROC quality and high Cas9 activity, respectively, to determine whether accepted PTEN evidence persists under stronger screen/technical quality filters. H256 and H257 test PTEN loss among TP53-intact research_signature_a-positive squamous lines and TP53-intact research_signature_a-positive high-aneuploidy lines, addressing lineage and chromosomal-instability boundaries while conditioning on the context that most clearly supported PTEN earlier. These are dataset-internal associations among measured variables or analysis-defined strata; they are not causal effects, single-gene knockout phenotypes, or external generalization claims. I applied the same acceptance rule as planned: a claim is accepted only if the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction, with every comparison cell containing at least 20 observations. Point estimates above threshold with lower bounds below threshold remain unresolved, and borderline negative or wide sparse results will not be upgraded. I deliberately avoided rerunning already tested claims that would reuse existing data and avoided adding unrelated closed unresolved probes, because additional multiplicity would weaken inference without directly addressing the central PTEN and TP53 robustness questions.

prompt:
Iteration 19/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

prompt:
Iteration 20/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

If future capacity existed, the highest-value next step would be a pre-specified robustness panel rather than additional exploratory subgroup mining: (1) PTEN-loss in TP53-intact research_signature_a-positive versus negative lines with adjustment or balancing for KEAP1, SMARCA4, lineage, aneuploidy, screen ROC, and Cas9 quality; (2) a pre-specified multivariable interaction assessment for TP53 loss by research_signature_a to test whether attenuation is robust to correlated technical and genomic features; and (3) a high-quality complete-case replication panel for the core SMARCA4, KEAP1, MSI-high, and TP53 associations. record.narrative: With no due assessments and no remaining validation budget, this explore stage registers a final pre-specified robustness panel rather than additional broad subgroup mining. The panel has two scientifically useful purposes. First, it asks whether the four strongest accepted marginal associations remain threshold-clearing in a simultaneously high-technical-quality subset defined by above-median Cas9 activity and above-median screen ROC quality: SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker dependency, TP53-loss weaker dependency, and MSI-high stronger dependency. These are dataset-internal associations, not causal knockout effects or generalizable biological claims. Second, it probes the least-settled claim, PTEN-loss dependency, in the most supported context after removing the three strongest accepted drivers and signature-negative backgrounds: TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a-positive lines. The high-quality screen ROC and high Cas9 complements were already tested; here I request lower-screen-quality and lower-Cas9-quality complements plus high- and lower-screen_nnmd strata. Falsifiable expectation: if PTEN-loss is a context-specific measured predictor rather than a screen-quality artifact, its stronger-dependency contrast should remain detectable in several of these complements, though it may be attenuated and possibly unresolved if cells are smaller. If low-quality strata are negative or unresolved, that would support describing PTEN context effects as quality-sensitive rather than uniform. Alternative interpretation for any accepted result remains residual confounding among correlated genomic, technical, and constructed-signature features. Direction convention: direction -1 claims a more negative exposed-minus-comparator dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; direction +1 claims less negative/more positive score, i.e. weaker dependency. Returned estimates and intervals are already signed to these hypothesis directions. I will interpret results only if all comparison cells contain at least 20 observations and the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds the 0.15 composite-dependency-unit threshold.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use

refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze stage only requests currently registered, evidence-free active claims. The selected eight claims are the final robustness panel from the persistent notes. H258-H261 test whether the four core measured associations remain threshold-clearing in a jointly high-quality technical subset: SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker dependency, TP53-loss weaker dependency, and MSI-high stronger dependency, all restricted to above-median Cas9 activity and above-median screen ROC. H262-H265 test the least-settled PTEN-loss context in TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a-positive lines under complementary or additional quality/screen strata: lower screen ROC, lower Cas9, higher screen_nnmd, and lower screen_nnmd. These are dataset-internal marginal comparisons among measured variables and analysis-defined strata, not causal, mechanistic, single-gene knockout, or generalization claims. Iteration 20/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All eight due results are valid Welch independent-cell comparisons with at least 20 observations in every comparison cell. The estimates and intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the claimed association. Applying the pre-specified threshold rule, I accept all eight because each signed estimate exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units and, more importantly, each signed 95% lower bound also exceeds +0.15. H258/R236: SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency in the jointly high Cas9/high screen-ROC subset, +0.700 [+0.568, +0.832]. H259/R237: KEAP1-loss weaker dependency in the same technical-quality subset, +0.706 [+0.568, +0.844]. H260/R238: TP53-loss weaker dependency in the same subset, +0.354 [+0.177, +0.532]; this clears the threshold but is less certain than the other core associations because the lower bound is only modestly above 0.15. H261/R239: MSI-high stronger dependency in the same subset, +0.684 [+0.469, +0.899]. Together, these support the robustness of the core measured associations under higher technical quality and make low Cas9 activity or poor screen-ROC quality an unlikely explanation for their presence in the supplied dataset. H262-H265/R240-R243 further accept PTEN-loss stronger dependency within TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds across complementary quality/screen strata: lower screen ROC +0.605 [+0.434, +0.777]; lower Cas9 activity +0.610 [+0.431, +0.789]; higher screen_nnmd +0.590 [+0.448, +0.732]; lower screen_nnmd +0.548 [+0.353, +0.744]. This complements earlier accepted high screen-ROC and high Cas9 PTEN contexts and strengthens a context-specific description of PTEN loss: associated with stronger composite dependency mainly in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds, not as a uniform global predictor. Important caveats remain. These are dataset-internal, noncausal associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata. Intervals are nominal and not fully adjusted for the larger history of exploratory subgroup testing, even though this final panel was limited and focused. Overlap at median cutpoints, missingness in Cas9/age/growth variables, and residual confounding among correlated genomic and technical features limit mechanistic or generalizable interpretation. No validation is requested because independent validation capacity is exhausted.

Iteration 20/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response

record.narrative:
No validation response deadlines or newly released validation results are listed; assessments_due is empty and independent validation capacity is exhausted. Therefore no claim statuses are changed at this synthesis stage and no validation is requested. The final synthesis applies the pre-specified rule that a measured comparison is scientifically meaningful only when the signed 95% Welch estimate and preferably the signed lower bound are clearly above +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered hypothesis direction. Returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction and are not re-multiplied. All conclusions are dataset-internal associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata, not causal knockout effects, mechanistic pathway claims, single-gene claims, or generalizable biomarker claims.

Supported findings. The strongest supported association in this supplied dataset is SMARCA4 loss with stronger composite dependency. H5/R5 gives signed effect +0.833 [0.767, 0.898], independently supported by R13 +0.795 [0.695, 0.896]. The association remains threshold-clearing in the jointly high Cas9-activity and high screen-ROC technical subset, H258/R236 +0.700 [0.568, 0.832], and across multiple accepted strata, including TP53-intact and KEAP1-intact backgrounds, KEAP1-loss backgrounds, lineage subtypes, screen-quality and Cas9-quality strata, growth-rate strata, and aneuploidy strata. KEAP1 loss is supported as a weaker-dependency marker. H7/R7 gives signed effect +0.832 [0.766, 0.897], independently supported by R26 +0.783 [0.688, 0.878], and it remains threshold-clearing in the same high-technical-quality subset, H259/R237 +0.706 [0.568, 0.844]. MSI-high is supported as a stronger-dependency marker. H41/R75 gives signed effect +0.792 [0.676, 0.907]. The TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact subset H90/R87 gives +0.745 [0.666, 0.825], independently supported by R93 +0.779 [0.675, 0.884], and the high-technical-quality subset H261/R239 gives +0.684 [0.469, 0.899]. TP53 loss is supported as a weaker-dependency marker overall: H3/R3 gives +0.423 [0.327, 0.520], independently supported by R39 +0.471 [0.334, 0.607], and the high-technical-quality subset H260/R238 gives +0.354 [0.177, 0.532]. The TP53 result is context-dependent: accepted interactions H104/R105 +0.812 [0.643, 0.981], validated by R120 +0.716 [0.463, 0.969], and H82/R77 +0.780 [0.492, 1.067], validated by R79 +0.570 [0.176, 0.965], support substantial attenuation of the TP53-loss weaker-dependency contrast in elevated constructed research-signature contexts. These interaction findings do not establish an opposite main effect inside those signature strata; they establish attenuation of the overall TP53-loss contrast.

Context-specific PTEN finding. PTEN loss is not supported as a uniform global predictor of stronger dependency. The broader contrast H50/R35 is signed +0.227 [0.131, 0.323], with lower bound below the +0.15 threshold. The most robust PTEN evidence is context-specific, concentrated in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds. H117/R121 in TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a-positive lines gives +0.576 [0.462, 0.689], independently supported by R131 +0.573 [0.405, 0.740]. Related accepted main effects include H58/R42 in TP53-intact lines +0.259 [0.169, 0.349], validated by R53 +0.294 [0.156, 0.431]; H67/R55 in TP53/KEAP1-intact lines +0.255 [0.165, 0.345], validated by R66 +0.305 [0.166, 0.444]; and H113/R116 in TP53-intact, research_signature_a nonnegative lines +0.534 [0.399, 0.669]. Accepted PTEN-loss interactions in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-conditioned backgrounds, including H140/R134, H152/R148, H168/R163, and H176/R176, support a larger PTEN-loss stronger-dependency contrast in signature-positive than in complementary signature-negative backgrounds. The final robustness panel H262-H265/R240-R243 accepted PTEN-loss stronger dependency across complementary screen-ROC, Cas9-quality, screen_nnmd-high, and screen_nnmd-low strata within triple-intact TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds, with lower bounds +0.434, +0.431, +0.448, and +0.353 respectively. The defensible conclusion is therefore context-specific: PTEN loss is associated with stronger composite dependency mainly in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds, not as a homogeneous global measured predictor.

Negative or non-supported findings. Under the same threshold rule, many registered comparisons do not provide scientifically meaningful evidence in their registered directions. These include lineage subtype H1/R1, KRAS mutation H2/R2, MTAP loss H4/R4, PIK3CA mutation H6/R6, MYC amplification H8/R8, constructed markers research_marker_d/e/f H9-H11/R9-R11, STK11 loss H18/R32, ARID1A loss H20/R34, RB1 loss H22/R36, BRCA2 loss H39/R38, NF1 loss H40/R74, sex H42/R76, media-serum contrast H43/R52, BRAF V600E H53/R60, EGFR amplification H54/R61, ERBB2 amplification H55/R62, SMAD4 loss H56/R63, APC mutation H96/R100 and APC-Wnt interaction H97/R101, screen batch H81/R72, CRISPR-library main contrasts H23/R37 and H33/R78, and matched omics coverage H35/R92. Many tested interactions for SMARCA4, KEAP1, MSI-high, TP53, and PTEN with lineage, library, age, ploidy, MYC expression, growth rate, screen quality, research-marker, or constructed-signature contexts were negative or did not clear the threshold. CDKN2A-loss contrasts were consistently subthreshold or too imprecise to support a meaningful stronger-dependency association. These negative findings are dataset-internal and do not establish causal nullity or absence in other datasets.

Unresolved uncertainty. Several questions remain genuinely unresolved because of sparse cells, low precision, or lack of valid returned evidence. MSI-high within TP53-loss lines remains unresolved: H93/R94 gives +0.884 [0.455, 1.313] and independent validation R106 gives +0.628 [0.032, 1.225], with validation lower bound below threshold. Broad PTEN-loss lineage main effects remain unresolved: adenocarcinoma H224/R202 +0.207 [0.097, 0.317], squamous H225/R203 +0.276 [0.080, 0.472], TP53-intact adenocarcinoma H236/R212 +0.231 [0.128, 0.333], and TP53-intact squamous H237/R213 +0.328 [0.141, 0.515]. Some PTEN triple-intact or aneuploidy-conditioned contrasts without strong research_signature_a conditioning remain unresolved, including H243/R222 and H248/R223. H146/R138 and H205/R185 are unresolved PTEN contrasts in quality or signature-c contexts. Other registered probes, such as some screen-quality, Cas9-quality, age, library, batch, and research_signature_c comparisons, have no valid returned evidence or remain too underpowered for assessment. Missingness or complete-case filtering in Cas9 activity, age, growth rate, and screen-quality variables further limits certainty in quality-stratified claims. Multiplicity from broad exploratory subgroup testing means the nominal 95% intervals are not fully adjusted for the full history of comparisons, although the final panels were more limited and pre-specified. Therefore all accepted effects should be described as measured associations in this supplied dataset, with biological interpretation and external generalizability unresolved.

Iteration 21/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.
