record.narrative: All nine newly delivered comparisons are valid Welch independent-cell tests with every comparison cell at least 20 observations, and all estimates/intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. Applying the pre-specified dataset-internal rule that an effect is scientifically meaningful only when the signed 95 percent lower bound is clearly above +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction: H286/R264 accepts (PTEN-loss stronger dependency within TP53-intact, research_signature_a nonnegative, research_signature_c negative; +0.582 [0.408,0.757]), H287/R265 accepts (PTEN-by-research_signature_a interaction within TP53-intact, research_signature_c negative; +0.563 [0.334,0.792]), H288/R266 accepts (PTEN-loss stronger dependency within TP53-intact, research_signature_a nonnegative, MSI-nonhigh; +0.546 [0.410,0.681]), and H289/R267 accepts (PTEN-by-research_signature_a interaction within TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh; +0.515 [0.348,0.682]). Together these results close the key active question about whether the PTEN research_signature_a context depends on research_signature_c positivity or MSI-high overlap: the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency contrast remains large and threshold-clearing when research_signature_c is below its median and when MSI-high lines are excluded. H292/R270 accepts (SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency within PTEN-loss lines; +0.738 [0.535,0.942]), H293/R271 accepts (KEAP1-loss weaker dependency within PTEN-loss lines; +0.717 [0.519,0.915]), and H294/R272 accepts (TP53-loss weaker dependency within PTEN-loss lines; +0.559 [0.274,0.844]), showing that the robust core associations remain meaningful even after conditioning on PTEN-loss status. H290/R268 remains unresolved because TP53 loss within MSI-high lines has a positive signed point estimate (+0.301) consistent with weaker dependency but an imprecise interval crossing zero and below threshold (-0.129 to 0.732) with a small exposed cell (n=24). H291/R269 also remains unresolved because the MSI-high-by-TP53-loss interaction has a signed point estimate below threshold (+0.123) and a broad interval (-0.316 to 0.563); the interval does not clearly rule out a meaningful effect in the claimed direction. These imprecise results do not overturn the robust global MSI-high stronger-dependency association, but they maintain that the MSI-high/TP53-loss stratum is not dataset-internal resolved. Audit considerations: these are dataset-internal measured associations among measured predictors and constructed signatures, not causal knockout or mechanistic claims; research signatures and cutoffs are analysis-defined and possibly correlated; many subgroup/interaction tests have been explored, so nominal 95 percent intervals are not fully family-wise corrected. The accepted effects are large enough that chance alone is less plausible, but generalizability and biological interpretation remain unresolved. No validation request is made because independent validation capacity is exhausted (remaining_new_requests=0).

prompt:
Iteration 23/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Acceptance rule: valid Welch cells with each cell n>=20 and signed lower bound clearly >+0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction; borderline lower bounds treated as unresolved, especially when cell counts are small. \n\nNewly accepted PTEN refinement: H286 and H287 show that the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency context tied to TP53-intact and research_signature_a nonnegative status extends into research_signature_c-negative backgrounds (R264 +0.582 [0.408,0.757]; R265 +0.563 [0.334,0.792]). H288 and H289 show the same PTEN context remains threshold-clear when MSI-high lines are excluded (R266 +0.546 [0.410,0.681]; R267 +0.515 [0.348,0.682]). This strengthens the narrow PTEN conclusion: PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency mainly in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive analysis-defined backgrounds; the association does not appear to be driven solely by overlap with high research_signature_c or MSI-high status. Still, these are dataset-internal, possibly overfitted subgroup contexts, not generalizable biomarker claims. \n\nNewly accepted robustness checks in PTEN-loss lines: H292 accepts SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency within PTEN-loss lines (+0.738 [0.535,0.942]); H293 accepts KEAP1-loss weaker dependency within PTEN-loss lines (+0.717 [0.519,0.915]); H294 accepts TP53-loss weaker dependency within PTEN-loss lines (+0.559 [0.274,0.844]). These do not overturn global MSI-high stronger-dependency evidence but keep the TP53-loss MSI stratum ambiguous. \n\nOverall accepted core associations remain: SMARCA4 loss = stronger dependency; KEAP1 loss = weaker dependency; MSI-high = stronger dependency overall; TP53 loss = weaker dependency overall but attenuated/reversed in elevated research_signature_a and research_signature_b contexts; PTEN loss = context-specific stronger dependency concentrated in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds, now shown robust to research_signature_c-negative and MSI-nonhigh exclusions. The immediate active untested claims remain H286 and H287, which test whether the PTEN-loss context tied to TP53-intact and research_signature_a-positive status extends into research_signature_c-negative backgrounds. I do not duplicate those active claims. The new panel is intended to address the two highest-value unresolved dataset-internal questions and to test whether the strongest core associations are robust within PTEN-loss lines. First, PTEN loss is not supported as a homogeneous global stronger-dependency marker, but accepted evidence concentrates in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-positive backgrounds. The new PTEN claims test whether that context survives exclusion of MSI-high, either as a main effect or as a research_signature_a interaction. This is important because the accepted PTEN strata are broad and MSI-high itself is a strong stronger-dependency marker; a clean negative or positive result would clarify whether PTEN context is independent of MSI status. Second, MSI-high is robust globally and in clean co-mutation backgrounds, but its TP53-loss stratum is uncertain. I therefore register TP53 loss within MSI-high lines and an MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction to test whether TP53 status modifies the MSI-high association, rather than relying only on the already returned broad MSI-within-TP53-loss estimates. Newly accepted H286/R264, H287/R265, H288/R266, and H289/R267 show that the PTEN research_signature_a context remains threshold-clearing in research_signature_c-negative and MSI-nonhigh backgrounds, weakening concern that it is driven solely by high research_signature_c or MSI-high overlap. record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no validation response deadlines are listed. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so I make no status changes in this synthesis. The final synthesis uses the current ledger and the pre-specified dataset-internal rule: an effect is scientifically meaningful only when the signed estimate exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction and the signed 95 percent Welch lower bound is clearly above 0.15, with at least 20 observations per comparison cell. Returned estimates and intervals are interpreted as already signed and were not re-multiplied. More negative dependency_composite values mean stronger dependency; therefore, accepted direction -1 effects correspond to stronger dependency, while accepted direction +1 effects correspond to weaker dependency. All conclusions below are dataset-internal measured associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata, not causal knockout effects, mechanistic claims, pathway claims, or generalizable biomarker claims.

SMARCA4 loss is the strongest and most internally stable association with stronger dependency. The global accepted comparison H5/R5 gives signed effect +0.833 [0.767,0.898], and independent validation R13 gives +0.795 [0.695,0.896]. The association remains threshold-clearing across many strata, including KEAP1-intact and KEAP1-loss backgrounds H13/R14 and H24/R19, lineage-specific comparisons H78/R69 and H79/R70, complete RNA/DNA/CRISPR QC lines H266/R244, high-Cas9/high-screen-ROC technical quality H258/R236, screen-quality, growth-rate, age, aneuploidy, ploidy, emt, and research-signature strata. Registered interactions asking whether the SMARCA4 association changes by KEAP1-loss status, lineage, library, research markers, MYC expression, screen quality, age, ploidy, or constructed signatures were mostly negative or did not clear the threshold, for example H25/R20 with validation R80, H44/R49, H47/R73, H60/R46, H74/R91, and H169/R164. The defensible conclusion is that SMARCA4-loss status is strongly associated with stronger composite dependency within this supplied dataset.

KEAP1 loss is strongly supported as a weaker-dependency association. The global accepted comparison H7/R7 gives signed effect +0.832 [0.766,0.897], and independent validation R26 gives +0.783 [0.688,0.878]. KEAP1-loss main effects remain accepted in SMARCA4-intact and SMARCA4-loss backgrounds H14/R15 and H31/R24, complete QC lines H267/R245, high-Cas9/high-screen-ROC lines H259/R237, and multiple lineage, screen-quality, growth-rate, signature, ploidy, and co-mutation strata. The reciprocal interaction tests with SMARCA4-loss status do not provide evidence for meaningful effect modification: H25/R20 with validation R80 and H26/R21 with validation R107 are not accepted. Other interactions with lineage, library, research signatures, hypoxia, MYC, screen quality, and age are negative or unresolved. The dataset conclusion is that KEAP1-loss status is robustly associated with weaker dependency within this supplied dataset.

MSI-high is supported as a stronger-dependency association overall. The global comparison H41/R75 gives signed effect +0.792 [0.676,0.907]. A key clean co-mutation background is TP53-, KEAP1-, and SMARCA4-intact, where H90/R87 gives +0.745 [0.666,0.825] and validation R93 gives +0.779 [0.675,0.884]. The association remains accepted in lineage-specific comparisons H108/R111 and H109/R112, complete QC lines H269/R247, high-screen-ROC lines H261/R239, and research_signature_c-positive backgrounds H279/R257. However, the MSI-high-within-TP53-loss stratum remains uncertain. H93/R94 has a large signed point estimate +0.884 [0.455,1.313], but independent validation R106 gives +0.628 [0.032,1.225], with a lower bound below the 0.15 threshold. The reciprocal H291/R269 interaction is also imprecise and below threshold. Thus MSI-high is a robust dataset-internal stronger-dependency association overall, but its dependence on TP53-loss status is not resolved.

TP53 loss is supported overall as a weaker-dependency association, but the association is context-dependent. The global comparison H3/R3 gives signed effect +0.423 [0.327,0.520], and validation R39 gives +0.471 [0.334,0.607]. The main effect remains accepted across many clean, high-quality, screen-quality, growth-rate, age, and signature backgrounds, including H268/R246, H260/R238, H278/R256, and many lineage and stratum-specific comparisons. The accepted global effect should not be interpreted as uniform. Accepted interactions show attenuation or apparent reversal of the weaker-dependency TP53-loss contrast in elevated constructed-signature contexts. In research_signature_a nonnegative backgrounds, H104/R105 gives signed interaction +0.812 [0.643,0.981], with validation R120 +0.716 [0.463,0.969]. In research_signature_b-positive backgrounds, H82/R77 gives signed interaction +0.780 [0.492,1.067], with validation R79 +0.570 [0.176,0.965]. These signed positive interaction estimates mean that, relative to the complement, the raw TP53-loss effect shifts opposite to the global weaker-dependency contrast in those signature-positive backgrounds. They do not establish an accepted main TP53-loss stronger-dependency effect inside those strata. Research_signature_c interaction H91/R88 is not supported. The best supported TP53 conclusion is that TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency overall, but this association is attenuated or shifted in high research_signature_a and high research_signature_b backgrounds.

PTEN loss is the key context-specific finding. It is not supported as a homogeneous global stronger-dependency marker. The closest global PTEN-loss contrast H50/R35 gives signed effect +0.227 [0.131,0.323], but the lower bound is below 0.15, so it is not accepted as scientifically meaningful under the pre-specified rule. The most robust PTEN evidence is in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-nonnegative backgrounds. Accepted main effects include H58/R42 in TP53-intact lines +0.259 [0.169,0.349], validated by R53 +0.294 [0.156,0.431]; H67/R55 in TP53- and KEAP1-intact lines +0.255 [0.165,0.345], validated by R66 +0.305 [0.166,0.444]; H113/R116 in TP53-intact, research_signature_a nonnegative lines +0.534 [0.399,0.669]; and H117/R121 in TP53-, KEAP1-, and SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a nonnegative lines +0.576 [0.462,0.689], validated by R131 +0.573 [0.405,0.740]. Accepted interactions reinforce the same background dependence, including H140/R134, H152/R148, H168/R163, H192/R176, H271/R249, and H285/R263. The newly returned research_signature_c and MSI exclusions clarify the context further: H286/R264 +0.582 [0.408,0.757] and H287/R265 +0.563 [0.334,0.792] support the PTEN-loss and PTEN-by-research_signature_a effects in TP53-intact, research_signature_c-negative lines; H288/R266 +0.546 [0.410,0.681] and H289/R267 +0.515 [0.348,0.682] support the same effects when MSI-high lines are excluded. This means the accepted PTEN association is not driven solely by overlap with high research_signature_c or MSI-high status. It remains narrow and context-conditional. Borderline PTEN effects without strong research_signature_a conditioning remain unresolved, for example H280/R258 and H282/R260. Conditioning on PTEN-loss status does not eliminate the strongest core associations: H292/R270 accepts SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency within PTEN-loss lines +0.738 [0.535,0.942], H293/R271 accepts KEAP1-loss weaker dependency within PTEN-loss lines +0.717 [0.519,0.915], and H294/R272 accepts TP53-loss weaker dependency within PTEN-loss lines +0.559 [0.274,0.844].

Negative or non-supported findings. Under the same threshold and precision rule, many measured predictors do not support meaningful differences in the registered directions. These include lineage subtype H1/R1, KRAS mutation H2/R2, MTAP loss H4/R4, PIK3CA mutation H6/R6, MYC amplification H8/R8, constructed markers research_marker_d/e/f H9/R9, H10/R10, and H11/R11, STK11 loss H18/R32, ARID1A loss H20/R34, RB1 loss H22/R36, BRCA2 loss H39/R38, NF1 loss H40/R74, sex H42/R76, media-serum contrast H43/R52, BRAF V600E H53/R60, EGFR amplification H54/R61, ERBB2 amplification H55/R62, SMAD4 loss H56/R63, APC mutation H96/R100 and APC-Wnt interaction H97/R101, screen batch H81/R72, CRISPR-library contrasts H23/R37 and H33/R78, matched omics coverage H35/R92, and CDKN2A-loss contrasts H19/R33, H52/R45, H57/R41, and H92/R89. Many interactions for SMARCA4, KEAP1, TP53, MSI-high, and PTEN with lineage, library, age, ploidy, MYC expression, growth rate, screen quality, research markers, or other constructed-signature contexts were negative or did not clear the threshold. These are dataset-internal negative evidence under the tested contrasts, not proof of causal nullity or absence in other datasets.

Unresolved uncertainty remains for several targeted issues. First, the MSI-high effect inside TP53-loss lines is not resolved: H93/R94 is broad, validation R106 has a lower bound below threshold, H290/R268 is imprecise with small exposed n=24, and H291/R269 is below threshold with a broad interval. Second, PTEN-loss lineage effects remain unresolved because of borderline lower bounds and sparse cells: adenocarcinoma H224/R202, squamous H225/R203, TP53-intact adenocarcinoma H236/R212, TP53-intact squamous H237/R213, and the PTEN squamous-versus-adenocarcinoma interaction within TP53-intact, research_signature_a nonnegative lines H273/R251. Third, several clean-background PTEN contrasts are borderline unresolved, including H280/R258, H282/R260, H243/R222, and H248/R223, and several probes lack valid returned evidence. Fourth, some accepted stratum-specific effects rely on relatively small exposed cells, and complete-QC, lineage, serum, ploidy, Cas9-quality, screen-quality, and signature strata may encode selection or correlated measured features. Missingness in Cas9 activity, age, growth rate, and screen-quality variables further limits certainty in quality-stratified claims. Finally, the long exploratory subgroup history means nominal 95 percent intervals are not fully corrected for multiplicity; the accepted large effects remain persuasive within this dataset, but external reproducibility is still the strongest evidence check.

The most informative next analysis is a pre-specified, adjusted multivariable analysis in an independent or holdout panel focused on two questions: first, PTEN-loss contrast conditional on TP53-intact and research_signature_a-positive status, ideally with a PTEN-loss by research_signature_a interaction adjusted for MSI-high, research_signature_c, screen quality, lineage, and ploidy; second, the MSI-high effect conditional on TP53-loss status, with a reciprocal MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction and adequate exposed MSI-high TP53-loss sample size. If further dataset-internal analysis were possible, the highest-value work would be cross-validated or permutation-calibrated adjusted interaction estimation rather than additional unadjusted subgroup fishing. Until such evidence is obtained, accepted conclusions should remain described as dataset-internal measured associations, with biological interpretation, mechanism, and generalizability unresolved.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Third, SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, and TP53 loss are robust core associations across many strata. I test their main effects within PTEN-loss lines as a cross-context robustness check: if these associations remain threshold-clear inside PTEN-loss lines, this supports the dataset-internal stability of the core markers rather than a broad PTEN-specific reorganization of dependency. record.narrative: No assessments are due, no validation response deadlines are pending, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore stage only registers targeted discovery refinements. The highest-value remaining dataset-internal ambiguity is the PTEN-loss lineage context. Existing evidence shows that PTEN loss is not a homogeneous global stronger-dependency marker, but accepted effects are concentrated in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-nonnegative backgrounds and remain after excluding MSI-high in aggregate. The lineage-specific PTEN contrasts H236/R212, H237/R213, and the PTEN-by-lineage interaction H232/R227 remain unresolved, largely because of borderline lower bounds and possible contamination by MSI-high status. These new claims are refinements of those specific unresolved parents rather than broad subgroup fishing. I propose PTEN-loss mean_difference among TP53-intact adenocarcinoma excluding MSI-high and among TP53-intact squamous excluding MSI-high, direction -1, because more negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency and prior accepted PTEN effects in TP53-intact contexts point in that direction. The anticipated direction is negative, but the result may remain attenuated because these contrasts do not condition on research_signature_a; research_signature_a-negative PTEN-loss lines may have little PTEN contrast. The formal PTEN-by-squamous-vs-adenocarcinoma interaction within TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh lines tests whether the accepted PTEN context differs by lineage. I anticipate squamous PTEN-loss lines may show a stronger negative contrast than adenocarcinoma lines because the accepted research_signature_a-positive squamous PTEN effect H256/R234 is numerically larger than the accepted adenocarcinoma effect H209/R189, but H273/R251 remains imprecise, so uncertainty is substantial. Alternative explanations include correlated lineage, signature, ploidy, or technical-quality structure rather than lineage modification. At analysis and appraise, I will accept only if every comparison cell has at least 20 observations and the signed 95% lower bound is clearly above +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction; borderline results will remain unresolved. All claims are dataset-internal measured associations only, not causal, mechanistic, single-gene, pathway, or generalizable conclusions.

prompt:
Iteration 24/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, no validation response deadline is pending, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze stage selects only the three active, previously registered claims H295-H297. These claims target the last major unresolved dataset-internal question in the PTEN-loss context: whether the supported PTEN-loss stronger-dependency association within TP53-intact backgrounds differs by lineage subtype after excluding MSI-high lines. H295 tests PTEN loss in TP53-intact adenocarcinoma excluding MSI-high; H296 tests PTEN loss in TP53-intact squamous excluding MSI-high; H297 tests whether the PTEN contrast differs by squamous versus adenocarcinoma within TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh lines. These are refinements of the unresolved PTEN lineage contrasts H236/R212, H237/R213, H224/R202, H225/R203, and H232/R227, and they avoid broad new subgroup fishing. For returned Welch results, all estimates and intervals are interpreted as already signed to the registered direction. Because more negative dependency_composite values mean stronger dependency, the registered direction -1 corresponds to stronger PTEN-loss dependency; H297 direction -1 corresponds to a stronger PTEN-loss effect in the squamous subgroup relative to its complement. At appraise, I will accept only if every comparison cell has at least 20 observations and the signed 95% lower bound is clearly above +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction. Borderline lower bounds or small exposed cells will remain unresolved. The results will be treated as dataset-internal measured associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata, not as causal, mechanistic, single-gene, pathway, or generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 24/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: R273 is a valid Welch independent-cell test with cells 144 and 913 and returns a signed PTEN-loss effect of +0.263 [0.157, 0.369] for the claim direction -1, corresponding to stronger dependency in PTEN-loss TP53-intact adenocarcinoma excluding MSI-high. I accept this as a dataset-internal association under the stated threshold because the point estimate and lower bound exceed 0.15 composite units in the claimed direction. However, the lower bound is only about 0.007 units above the threshold, so this should be treated as borderline and highly susceptible to multiplicity and residual confounding. R274 is valid with cells 55 and 376 and gives +0.330 [0.143, 0.517]. The point estimate is above threshold, but the lower bound is below 0.15, so the evidence does not establish that the true effect exceeds the threshold. I leave H296 unresolved and defer it, because the squamous comparison is imprecise and not conditioned on research_signature_a or other correlated context features. R275 tests the squamous-versus-adenocarcinoma interaction within TP53-intact MSI-nonhigh lines and gives +0.067 [-0.147, 0.281], below threshold and crossing zero. I reject H297. The apparent difference between H295 and H296 is not evidence for lineage modification; it is more plausibly sampling variation, precision loss, or correlated structure. The global PTEN-by-lineage interaction H232/R227 is also unsupported (+0.069 [-0.155, 0.293]), so I reassess H232 as reject and close it. H273 remains unresolved because it has a point estimate above threshold but a wide interval crossing zero; I defer it rather than reject, as it is a narrower research_signature_a-conditioned interaction. Audit concerns: H295-H297 are unadjusted subgroup contrasts embedded in a large exploratory program; research_signature_a, ploidy, quality metrics, MSI, lineage, and TP53 status are likely correlated, so these estimates cannot be interpreted as independent adjusted effects. H295's threshold-clearing margin is tiny, so even modest adjustment could alter it. The results are not causal, mechanistic, single-gene, pathway, or generalizable conclusions. No validation request is made because independent validation capacity is exhausted.

prompt:
Iteration 24/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Core accepted associations remain: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency, strongest globally H5/R5 with validation R13 and robust across strata; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency, H7/R7 with validation R26 and robust across strata; MSI-high is associated with stronger dependency globally H41/R75 and in clean TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4-intact background H90/R87 with validation R93, though MSI-high within TP53-loss remains unresolved; TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency overall H3/R3 with validation R39 but is attenuated or shifted in high research_signature_a and research_signature_b backgrounds H104/R105/R120 and H82/R77/R79. PTEN loss is not supported as a homogeneous global stronger-dependency marker, but the supported PTEN context is TP53-intact and especially research_signature_a-nonnegative backgrounds, with validated examples H58/R42/R53, H67/R55/R66, and H117/R121/R131, and further accepted refinements excluding signature_c-positive or MSI-high lines: H286/R264, H287/R265, H288/R266, and H289/R267. New result H295/R273 accepts PTEN-loss stronger dependency within TP53-intact adenocarcinoma excluding MSI-high, +0.263 [0.157, 0.369], but only borderline above threshold. New result H296/R274 remains unresolved in TP53-intact squamous excluding MSI-high, +0.330 [0.143, 0.517], because the lower bound is below 0.15. New result H297/R275 rejects the squamous-versus-adenocarcinoma PTEN interaction within TP53-intact MSI-nonhigh lines, +0.067 [-0.147, 0.281]; parent H232/R227 is also reassessed as reject. Thus lineage modification of the PTEN association is not supported in these contrasts, and differences between adenocarcinoma and squamous estimates may reflect precision, signature distribution, or confounding rather than real lineage modification. H273/R251 remains unresolved/deferred because the research_signature_a-conditioned squamous interaction has a point estimate above threshold but an interval crossing zero. Core SMARCA4, KEAP1, and TP53 associations remain accepted within PTEN-loss lines H292/R270, H293/R271, and H294/R272. Remaining unresolved issues include PTEN lineage contexts, MSI-high within TP53-loss, several borderline PTEN clean-background contrasts, and probes lacking valid returned evidence. record.narrative:
No assessments_due are pending and no validation response deadlines are listed. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no new validation request is made and the controller-maintained accepted claim set is left unchanged. The final synthesis therefore assesses the evidence already present in the ledger under the pre-specified dataset-internal rule: a measured contrast is called scientifically meaningful only when the returned estimate and signed 95 percent Welch lower bound are clearly above the absolute threshold of 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction, with valid cell counts of at least 20. Returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the hypothesis direction and are not re-multiplied. Because more negative dependency_composite values mean stronger dependency, accepted direction -1 contrasts indicate stronger dependency, while accepted direction +1 contrasts indicate weaker dependency. All conclusions are dataset-internal measured associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata; they are not causal knockout effects, mechanistic claims, single-gene interpretations, pathway claims, or generalizable clinical or biological conclusions.

The strongest supported finding is SMARCA4-loss status as a predictor of stronger composite dependency. The global SMARCA4-loss contrast H5/R5 gives a signed effect of +0.833 composite units, interval [0.767, 0.898], and independent validation R13 gives +0.795, interval [0.695, 0.896]. This association remains threshold-clearing across many independent-looking strata: KEAP1-intact background H13/R14; KEAP1-loss background H24/R40 with validation R40 +0.926 [0.741, 1.110]; adenocarcinoma H79/R70 and squamous H78/R69; complete RNA-DNA-CRISPR QC lines H266/R244; high Cas9 activity plus high screen ROC AUC H258/R236; high screen_nnmd H187/R171; low screen_nnmd H210/R190; screen_doubling_time strata H212/R192 and H227/R198; age strata H181/R204, H218/R207; research_signature_a nonnegative and negative strata H193/R177 and H206/R186; research_signature_c-positive H276/R254; aneuploidy-high and aneuploidy-low H238/R214 and H246/R220; ploidy-high H275/R253; and EMT-positive H124/R128. Registered interaction tests asking whether SMARCA4-loss association varies by KEAP1-loss status, lineage, library, screen quality, age, ploidy, aneuploidy, MYC expression, research markers, research signatures, or other measured contexts mostly fail to clear the threshold. Examples include H25/R20 with validation R80, H44/R49, H47/R73, H60/R46, H74/R91, H134/R143, H169/R164, H172/R167, H184 unresolved, and H248/R223 unresolved. The defensible dataset conclusion is robust: SMARCA4-loss status is strongly associated with stronger dependency_composite within this supplied dataset, with no well-supported context modifier identified under the tested contrasts.

KEAP1-loss status is robustly supported as a weaker-dependency association. The global contrast H7/R7 gives +0.832 [0.766, 0.897], and independent validation R26 gives +0.783 [0.688, 0.878]. Main effects remain accepted in SMARCA4-intact H14/R15 and H38/R29, SMARCA4-loss H31/R24, TP53-loss H100/R98 and TP53-intact H15/R16, lineage-specific comparisons H86/R83 and H87/R84, complete QC lines H267/R245, high Cas9 activity plus high screen ROC AUC H259/R237, high screen_nnmd H188/R172, screen_doubling_time strata H213/R193 and H228/R199, age strata H182/R205 and H219/R208, research_signature_a strata H194/R178 and H207/R187, research_signature_c-positive H277/R255, EMT-positive H125/R129, hypoxia strata H110/R113 and H121/R125, and aneuploidy strata H239/R215 and H247/R221. The reciprocal SMARCA4-by-KEAP1 interaction tests do not support meaningful effect modification: H26/R21 with validation R107 and H25/R20 with validation R80 fail to clear the threshold. Other interactions with lineage, library, screen quality, hypoxia, MYC expression, research signatures, age, ploidy, and other contexts either do not clear the threshold or remain unresolved. The defensible dataset conclusion is robust: KEAP1-loss status is strongly associated with weaker dependency_composite within this supplied dataset.

MSI-high status is supported as a stronger-dependency association overall. The global contrast H41/R75 gives +0.792 [0.676, 0.907]. In the cleaner background TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, and SMARCA4-intact, H90/R87 gives +0.745 [0.666, 0.825], with independent validation R93 +0.779 [0.675, 0.884]. The association is also accepted in adenocarcinoma H108/R111 and squamous H109/R112, complete QC lines H269/R247, high screen quality H261/R239, screen_nnmd-high H189/R173, screen_doubling_time strata H214/R194 and H229/R200, Cas9-activity strata H155/R151 and H156/R152, age strata H220/R209 and H231/R211, research_signature_c-positive H279/R257, EMT-positive contexts, and aneuploidy strata H240/R216 and H244/R218. However, the specificity of MSI-high effects inside TP53-loss lines remains unresolved. H93/R94 has a large signed point estimate +0.884 [0.455, 1.313], but independent validation R106 is +0.628 [0.032, 1.225], with lower bound below the 0.15 threshold. H290/R268 within MSI-high lines for TP53 loss is imprecise with exposed n=24, and the reciprocal interaction H291/R269 is below threshold with a broad interval. The best dataset-internal conclusion is that MSI-high status is strongly associated with stronger dependency overall and in clean co-mutation backgrounds, but whether the effect differs materially when TP53 is lost is not resolved.

TP53-loss status is supported overall as a weaker-dependency association, but the association is context-dependent rather than uniform. The global contrast H3/R3 gives +0.423 [0.327, 0.520], and independent validation R39 gives +0.471 [0.334, 0.607]. The main effect is accepted in many strata, including KEAP1-intact H15/R16, SMARCA4-intact H29/R22 and H36/R27, KEAP1-loss H30/R23, lineage-specific H88/R85 and H89/R86, complete QC lines H268/R246, high Cas9 plus high screen ROC AUC H260/R238, high screen_nnmd H190/R174, screen_doubling_time strata H215/R195 and H230/R201, age strata H183/R206 and H221/R210, research_signature_c-positive H278/R256, and EMT-positive H126/R130. The global association is attenuated or reversed in elevated constructed-signature contexts. In research_signature_a nonnegative lines, H104/R105 gives a signed interaction +0.812 [0.643, 0.981] with validation R120 +0.716 [0.463, 0.969]; in research_signature_a >=1 lines, H65/R48 gives +0.590 [0.338, 0.842]. In research_signature_b >=1 lines, H82/R77 gives a signed interaction +0.780 [0.492, 1.067] with validation R79 +0.570 [0.176, 0.965]. These are interactions, not accepted main effects inside those strata; they indicate that the raw TP53-loss contrast in the signature-positive subgroup differs from the complement in the registered stronger-dependency direction. Research_signature_c interaction H91/R88 is not supported. The defensible dataset conclusion is: TP53-loss status is associated with weaker dependency overall, but this association is attenuated or shifted in high research_signature_a and high research_signature_b backgrounds.

PTEN-loss status is the principal context-specific finding. It is not supported as a homogeneous global stronger-dependency marker. The closest global PTEN-loss contrast H50/R35 has signed point estimate +0.227 [0.131, 0.323], but the lower bound does not clear 0.15, so it is not accepted under the pre-specified rule. The most robust PTEN evidence is in TP53-intact backgrounds, especially when combined with research_signature_a-nonnegative status and excluding MSI-high. Accepted main effects include TP53-intact H58/R42 +0.259 [0.169, 0.349] with validation R53 +0.294 [0.156, 0.431]; TP53- and KEAP1-intact H67/R55 +0.255 [0.165, 0.345] with validation R66 +0.305 [0.166, 0.444]; TP53-intact research_signature_a nonnegative H113/R116 +0.534 [0.399, 0.669]; and TP53-, KEAP1-, SMARCA4-intact, research_signature_a nonnegative H117/R121 +0.576 [0.462, 0.689] with validation R131 +0.573 [0.405, 0.740]. Accepted interactions reinforce the same context dependence: H140/R134, H152/R148, H168/R163, H192/R176, H271/R249, and H285/R263. The newer exclusions show the accepted PTEN association is not driven solely by MSI-high or research_signature_c-positive overlap: H286/R264 +0.582 [0.408, 0.757], H287/R265 +0.563 [0.334, 0.792], H288/R266 +0.546 [0.410, 0.681], and H289/R267 +0.515 [0.348, 0.682] remain accepted when research_signature_c-positive or MSI-high lines are excluded. The most recent lineage probes refine but do not resolve lineage modification. H295/R273 accepts PTEN loss in TP53-intact adenocarcinoma excluding MSI-high, +0.263 [0.157, 0.369], but the lower bound is only slightly above threshold. H296/R274 remains unresolved in TP53-intact squamous excluding MSI-high, +0.330 [0.143, 0.517], because the lower bound is below threshold. H297/R275 rejects the squamous-versus-adenocarcinoma PTEN interaction within TP53-intact MSI-nonhigh lines, +0.067 [-0.147, 0.281], and the broader PTEN-by-lineage interaction H232/R227 is also unsupported. H273/R251 remains unresolved for the research_signature_a-conditioned squamous interaction. Thus, PTEN-loss status is best described as a context-conditional stronger-dependency association in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-nonnegative backgrounds, with no robust evidence that lineage subtype independently modifies the PTEN association in the tested contrasts. Core SMARCA4, KEAP1, and TP53 associations persist within PTEN-loss lines: H292/R270 +0.738 [0.535, 0.942], H293/R271 +0.717 [0.519, 0.915], and H294/R272 +0.559 [0.274, 0.844].

Negative or non-supported findings are numerous. Under the same threshold and precision rule, measured statuses do not support meaningful dependency differences in the registered directions for lineage subtype H1/R1, KRAS mutation H2/R2, MTAP loss H4/R4, PIK3CA mutation H6/R6, MYC amplification H8/R8, constructed research markers d/e/f H9/R9, H10/R10, H11/R11, STK11 loss H18/R32, ARID1A loss H20/R34, RB1 loss H22/R36, BRCA2 loss H39/R38, NF1 loss H40/R74, sex H42/R76, media-serum contrast H43/R52, BRAF V600E H53/R60, EGFR amplification H54/R61, ERBB2 amplification H55/R62, SMAD4 loss H56/R63, APC mutation H96/R100, APC-by-Wnt interaction H97/R101, screen batch H81/R72, CRISPR-library contrasts H23/R37 and H33/R78, and matched omics coverage H35/R92. CDKN2A-loss contrasts are repeatedly not accepted as meaningful in the registered stronger-dependency direction, including H19/R33, H52/R45, H57/R41, and H92/R89. Many interaction probes for SMARCA4, KEAP1, TP53, MSI-high, and PTEN against lineage, library, screen batch, age, ploidy, growth rate, MYC expression, screen quality, research markers, and other constructed-signature contexts are negative or below threshold. These are dataset-internal negative evidence under the tested unadjusted contrasts, not causal nullities or proof of absence in other populations.

Important unresolved uncertainty remains. The MSI-high effect inside TP53-loss lines is not resolved because of imprecision and borderline validation. PTEN-loss lineage effects remain unresolved, especially H296/R274, H237/R213, H225/R203, and H273/R251. Several clean-background PTEN contrasts are borderline unresolved, including H280/R258, H282/R260, H243/R222, H248/R223, and H296/R274. Some probes lack valid returned evidence and remain unresolved. Multiple accepted stratum-specific effects rely on relatively small exposed cells or overlap with correlated measured features such as research_signature_a, research_signature_c, MSI-high, ploidy, aneuploidy, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and lineage. Missingness in Cas9 activity, age, growth rate, and screen-quality variables also limits certainty in quality-stratified claims. The long exploratory subgroup history means nominal 95 percent intervals are not fully corrected for multiplicity; large accepted effects remain persuasive within this dataset, but they should not be treated as independent confirmed effects across all strata.

The most informative next analysis would be a pre-specified adjusted analysis in an independent or holdout panel. It should jointly estimate PTEN-loss effects conditional on TP53-intact and research_signature_a-positive status, with a PTEN-loss by research_signature_a interaction adjusted for MSI-high, research_signature_c, lineage subtype, ploidy, aneuploidy, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and other correlated features. It should also test the MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction with adequate exposed MSI-high and TP53-loss sample size. If further dataset-internal analysis were possible, the best replacement for additional unadjusted subgroup fishing would be cross-validated or permutation-calibrated adjusted interaction estimation. Until such adjusted evidence is obtained, accepted conclusions should remain described as dataset-internal measured associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata; biological interpretation, mechanism, causal knockout interpretation, single-gene interpretation, pathway interpretation, and generalizability remain unsupported.

prompt:
Iteration 25/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.
