record.narrative: With independent-validation capacity exhausted and no scheduled validation response pending, this explore stage registers only focused dataset-internal discovery refinements. The most informative remaining ambiguity is the PTEN-loss context model. Prior evidence does not support PTEN loss as a homogeneous global stronger-dependency marker, but accepted contrasts concentrate in TP53-intact and research_signature_a-nonnegative backgrounds, including after excluding MSI-high in aggregate. The lineage context remains ambiguous: squamous and adenocarcinoma PTEN contrasts have overlapping but imprecise evidence, and the direct lineage interaction under research_signature_a conditioning remains unresolved. I therefore register two lineage-specific PTEN-loss mean-difference tests within TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh, research_signature_a-non-negative contexts: squamous and adenocarcinoma. The registered direction is -1 because more negative dependency_composite values mean stronger dependency; I anticipate raw exposed-minus-comparator differences negative, i.e., PTEN-loss lines have stronger dependency. These are refinements of H296 and H295, respectively. I also register the corresponding squamous-versus-adenocarcinoma interaction within the same eligible background, direction -1, to test whether the PTEN association is modified by lineage subtype after removing MSI-high contamination. I anticipate a more negative squamous PTEN contrast than adenocarcinoma contrast, but the prior direct interaction H273 was imprecise, so the result may be unresolved or below threshold. Finally, I register a negative-control PTEN-loss test in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-negative, MSI-nonhigh lines. The direction is still -1 to test a claimed stronger-dependency effect, but the anticipated direction is 0 because the existing TP53-intact research_signature_a-negative contrast H159 did not support a threshold-clearing PTEN effect. If this negative-control contrast is accepted, it would falsify or materially weaken the proposed research_signature_a-restricted PTEN context model; if it remains null or threshold-missed, that supports the context-restricted interpretation. At analysis and appraise, I will accept only if every comparison cell has at least 20 observations and the signed 95% Welch lower bound is clearly above the absolute threshold of 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction. Borderline or invalid cells will remain unresolved or be rejected. Plausible alternatives to any accepted lineage-specific PTEN effect include residual confounding by correlated measured features such as research_signature_c, ploidy, aneuploidy, screen quality, Cas9 activity, PTEN-loss prevalence differences across lineage, and unadjusted compositional differences in research_signature_a distribution. These are measured associations within the supplied dataset only, not causal, mechanistic, single-gene, pathway, or generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 25/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

prompt:
Iteration 25/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: R276 and R277 provide valid Welch evidence for the registered research_signature_a-restricted PTEN-loss context model: in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-non-negative, MSI-non-high lines, PTEN loss is associated with stronger composite dependency in both squamous H298 and adenocarcinoma H299, with signed lower bounds 0.456 and 0.318 respectively, clearly above the 0.15 absolute threshold. I accept both, but with caution because H298 has only 29 exposed lines, these are narrow exploratory strata, and correlated features may still confound the subgroup estimates. H300 rejects the corresponding squamous-versus-adenocarcinoma interaction: the signed point estimate is 0.201, but the interval includes zero and its lower bound is below the threshold, so the data do not support lineage modification of PTEN-loss association within this context. record.narrative:
No assessments are due, no validation response deadlines are pending, and independent validation capacity is exhausted. This final synthesis therefore reports the strongest dataset-internal evidence available in the supplied ledger. The decision rule is the pre-specified rule: a measured contrast is scientifically meaningful only when the returned signed estimate and signed 95 percent Welch lower bound are clearly above the absolute threshold of 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the registered direction, and every comparison cell has at least 20 valid observations. Returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the hypothesis direction and are not re-multiplied. Direction -1 means the exposed group has stronger dependency, while direction +1 means the exposed group has weaker dependency. All conclusions are unadjusted measured associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata within this supplied dataset. They are not causal knockout effects, mechanistic pathway claims, single-gene knockout interpretations, clinical effects, or generalizable biological conclusions.

Supported core finding 1: SMARCA4-loss status is robustly associated with stronger dependency_composite. The global contrast H5/R5 gives signed effect 0.833 composite units, interval 0.767 to 0.898, and independent validation R13 gives 0.795, interval 0.695 to 0.896. This association remains threshold-clearing across many independent-looking strata, including KEAP1-intact H13/R14, KEAP1-loss H24/R40 with validation R40, squamous H78/R69, adenocarcinoma H79/R70, complete RNA-DNA-CRISPR QC H266/R244, high Cas9 and high screen ROC AUC H258/R236, screen_nnmd-high H187/R171, screen_nnmd-low H210/R190, screen_doubling_time strata H212/R192 and H227/R198, age strata H181/R204 and H218/R207, research_signature_a strata H193/R177 and H206/R186, research_signature_c-positive H276/R254, aneuploidy strata H238/R214 and H246/R220, EMT-positive H124/R128, and several other accepted strata. Registered interaction tests asking whether SMARCA4-loss association is modified by KEAP1 loss, lineage, CRISPR library, screen quality, age, ploidy, aneuploidy, MYC expression, research signatures, or other measured contexts are largely unsupported or unresolved, including H25/R20 with validation R80, H26/R21 with validation R107, H44/R49, H47/R73, H60/R46, H74/R91, H134/R143, H169/R164, and H172/R167. The defensible conclusion is that SMARCA4-loss status is a very strong predictor of stronger composite dependency within this dataset, with no well-supported context modifier identified among the tested contrasts.

Supported core finding 2: KEAP1-loss status is robustly associated with weaker dependency_composite. The global contrast H7/R7 gives signed effect 0.832, interval 0.766 to 0.897, and independent validation R26 gives 0.783, interval 0.688 to 0.878. Accepted main effects are broad: SMARCA4-intact H14/R15 and H38/R29, SMARCA4-loss H31/R24, TP53-loss H100/R98, TP53-intact H15/R16, lineage-specific H86/R83 and H87/R84, complete QC H267/R245, high Cas9 and high screen ROC AUC H259/R237, screen_nnmd-high H188/R172, screen_doubling_time strata H213/R193 and H228/R199, age strata H182/R205 and H219/R208, research_signature_a strata H194/R178 and H207/R187, research_signature_c-positive H277/R255, EMT-positive H125/R129, hypoxia strata H110/R113 and H121/R125, and aneuploidy strata H239/R215 and H247/R221. Interaction tests for KEAP1-loss effect modification are not robust: reciprocal SMARCA4-by-KEAP1 interactions H25/R20 and H26/R21 fail with validation, lineage H45/R50 and H173 unresolved, library H48/R64, screen-quality H170/R165, MYC-expression H137/R286, and other tested contexts are unsupported. The defensible conclusion is that KEAP1-loss status is a robust predictor of weaker composite dependency within this dataset, with no well-supported independent effect modifier identified.

Supported core finding 3: MSI-high status is associated with stronger dependency_composite overall. The global contrast H41/R75 gives signed effect 0.792, interval 0.676 to 0.907. In the cleaner TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, SMARCA4-intact background, H90/R87 gives 0.745, interval 0.666 to 0.825, with independent validation R93 giving 0.779, interval 0.675 to 0.884. MSI-high effects remain accepted in lineage strata H108/R111 and H109/R112, complete QC H269/R247, high Cas9 and high screen ROC AUC H261/R239, screen_nnmd-high H189/R173, screen_doubling_time strata H214/R194 and H229/R200, Cas9-activity strata H155/R151 and H156/R152, age strata H220/R209 and H231/R211, research_signature_c-positive H279/R257, aneuploidy strata H240/R216 and H244/R218, and IFN-gamma strata H122/R126. However, the specificity of MSI-high status within TP53-loss lines remains unresolved. H93/R94 has a large point estimate 0.884, interval 0.455 to 1.313, but validation R106 gives 0.628, interval 0.032 to 1.225, whose lower bound is below the 0.15 threshold. The reciprocal TP53-loss effect within MSI-high H290/R268 is imprecise, and the MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction H291/R269 is unsupported. Thus the supported conclusion is that MSI-high status is associated with stronger dependency overall and in clean co-mutation backgrounds, but whether its effect is materially altered by TP53-loss status is not resolved.

Supported core finding 4: TP53-loss status is associated with weaker dependency_composite overall, but the association is context-dependent in constructed signature space. The global contrast H3/R3 gives signed effect 0.423, interval 0.327 to 0.520, with independent validation R39 giving 0.471, interval 0.334 to 0.607. Main effects are accepted in many strata, including KEAP1-intact H15/R16, SMARCA4-intact H29/R22 and H36/R27, KEAP1-loss H30/R23, lineage H88/R85 and H89/R86, complete QC H268/R246, high Cas9 and high screen ROC AUC H260/R238, screen_nnmd-high H190/R174, screen_doubling_time strata H215/R195 and H230/R201, age strata H183/R206 and H221/R210, research_signature_c-positive H278/R256, EMT-positive H126/R130, hypoxia H119/R123, and aneuploidy strata H241/R217 and H245/R219. The global weaker-dependency association is strongly modified by research_signature_a and research_signature_b contexts. Accepted interactions include H65/R48 with signed effect 0.590, interval 0.338 to 0.842, H104/R105 with signed effect 0.812, interval 0.643 to 0.981, and validation R120 giving 0.716, interval 0.463 to 0.969, plus H82/R77 with signed effect 0.780, interval 0.492 to 1.067, and validation R79 giving 0.570, interval 0.176 to 0.965. The corresponding signature-negative main effects are supported, for example H106/R109 gives 0.840, interval 0.759 to 0.922, and H85/R82 gives 0.556, interval 0.459 to 0.653, while signature-positive main effects are not cleanly accepted, for example H76/R67, H105/R108, H84/R81, and H158/R153 are rejected. The correct conclusion is that TP53-loss status is associated with weaker dependency in this dataset, especially in lower research_signature_a and lower research_signature_b backgrounds, but the global association is attenuated or direction-shifted in signature-positive backgrounds. These are association-level effect-modification results, not causal or mechanistic statements.

Supported core finding 5: PTEN-loss status is the principal context-specific predictor. It is not supported as a homogeneous global stronger-dependency marker under the threshold rule; the closest global test H50/R35 has signed point estimate 0.227, interval 0.131 to 0.323, with lower bound below 0.15. Accepted PTEN-loss stronger-dependency effects concentrate in TP53-intact backgrounds, especially when research_signature_a is nonnegative. Supported contrasts include TP53-intact H58/R42 with signed effect 0.259, interval 0.169 to 0.349, and validation R53; TP53- and KEAP1-intact H67/R55 with 0.255, interval 0.165 to 0.345, and validation R66; TP53-intact research_signature_a-nonnegative H113/R116 with 0.534, interval 0.399 to 0.669; and the clean TP53-, KEAP1-, SMARCA4-intact research_signature_a-nonnegative contrast H117/R121 with 0.576, interval 0.462 to 0.689, plus validation R131 giving 0.573, interval 0.405 to 0.740. Accepted interactions reinforce the same context dependence, including H140/R134, H152/R148, H168/R163, H192/R176, H271/R249, and H285/R263. The model is not merely driven by MSI-high or research_signature_c-positive overlap: PTEN contrasts excluding MSI-high remain accepted in H286/R266 and H288/R264, and PTEN interactions with research_signature_a remain accepted in the MSI-nonhigh background H289/R267. The most recent context-restricted lineage probes accept PTEN loss in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-nonnegative, MSI-nonhigh squamous H298/R276 with 0.687, interval 0.456 to 0.917, and adenocarcinoma H299/R277 with 0.486, interval 0.318 to 0.654, although H298 has only 29 exposed lines. The negative-control PTEN test H301/R279 in TP53-intact, research_signature_a-negative, MSI-nonhigh lines is rejected, with effect 0.031 and interval crossing zero, supporting the interpretation that the PTEN effect is concentrated in research_signature_a-nonnegative backgrounds rather than being a generic TP53-intact effect. Lineage is not a robust independent modifier: broad PTEN-by-lineage interaction H232/R227, MSI-nonhigh squamous interaction H297/R275, and context-restricted squamous interaction H300/R278 are unsupported. Some PTEN lineage estimates remain unresolved, especially H296/R274 with 0.330 and interval 0.143 to 0.517, H237/R213, H225/R203, and H273/R251. Therefore the defensible PTEN conclusion is that PTEN-loss status is associated with stronger dependency conditionally on TP53-intact and research_signature_a-nonnegative status, with MSI-high contamination excluded or controlled by stratum choice, but without robust evidence that lineage subtype independently modifies the PTEN association among the tested contrasts. Core SMARCA4, KEAP1, and TP53 associations also persist inside PTEN-loss lines: H292/R270, H293/R271, and H294/R272 are accepted, indicating that PTEN context does not eliminate the main SMARCA4-loss stronger-dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker-dependency, and TP53-loss weaker-dependency signals in the tested PTEN-loss subset.

Negative findings are broad but important. Under the same threshold and precision rule, measured statuses do not support meaningful dependency_composite differences in the registered directions for lineage subtype H1/R1, KRAS mutation H2/R2, MTAP loss H4/R4, PIK3CA mutation H6/R6, MYC amplification H8/R8, constructed research markers d, e, and f H9/R9, H10/R10, and H11/R11, STK11 loss H18/R32, ARID1A loss H20/R34, RB1 loss H22/R36, BRCA2 loss H39/R38, NF1 loss H40/R74, sex H42/R76, media-serum contrast H43/R52, BRAF V600E H53/R60, EGFR amplification H54/R61, ERBB2 amplification H55/R62, SMAD4 loss H56/R63, APC mutation H96/R100, APC-by-Wnt interaction H97/R101, screen batch contrasts H81/R72 and H223/R280, CRISPR-library contrasts H23/R37, H33/R78, and H34/R281, matched RNA-DNA omics coverage H35/R92, RNA-omics availability H63/R282, and DNA-omics availability H64/R283. CDKN2A-loss contrasts are repeatedly not accepted as meaningful in the registered stronger-dependency direction, including H19/R33, H52/R45, H57/R41, and H92/R89. Many interaction probes for SMARCA4, KEAP1, TP53, MSI-high, and PTEN against lineage, library, screen batch, age, ploidy, growth rate, MYC expression, screen quality, AXL expression, hypoxia, and other constructed-signature contexts are negative or below threshold, including H129/R284, H133/R285, H137/R286, and H138/R287. These negative results mean the tested unadjusted contrasts do not provide evidence for meaningful effects at the 0.15 threshold; they are not causal nullities or proof of absence in other populations.

Unresolved uncertainty remains in several places. The MSI-high effect inside TP53-loss lines is unresolved because of imprecision and borderline validation, especially H93/R94 with R106, H290/R268, and H291/R269. PTEN-loss lineage effects remain unresolved, with H296/R274, H237/R213, H225/R203, and H273/R251 not meeting the strict acceptance rule. Some clean-background PTEN contrasts are borderline unresolved, including H280/R258, H282/R260, H243/R222, and H248/R223. Several registered probes have no returned evidence in the ledger and remain unresolved, including some hypoxia, research_signature_c, age, and screen-batch interaction probes. Multiple accepted stratum-specific effects rely on relatively small exposed cells, especially some PTEN lineage and context-restricted contrasts, and correlated measured features such as research_signature_a, research_signature_c, MSI-high, ploidy, aneuploidy, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and lineage subtype may confound individual subgroup estimates. Missingness in Cas9 activity, age, growth rate, and screen-quality variables also limits certainty in quality-stratified claims. The long exploratory subgroup history means nominal 95 percent intervals are not fully corrected for multiplicity, so large accepted effects are persuasive within this dataset but should not be interpreted as independent confirmed effects across every tested stratum.

The most informative next analysis is not more unadjusted subgroup fishing in this same dataset. It should be a pre-specified adjusted analysis in an independent or holdout panel. The key PTEN question should be estimated with a joint model for PTEN-loss status, TP53-loss status, research_signature_a, their two-way and three-way interactions, and adjustment for MSI-high, research_signature_c, lineage subtype, ploidy, aneuploidy, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and screen kinetics. The key MSI-high question should estimate the MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction with adequate exposed MSI-high and TP53-loss sample size. If additional dataset-internal work were possible, the best replacement would be adjusted interaction estimation with cross-validation or permutation calibration rather than additional marginal stratum-specific Welch tests. Until such adjusted evidence exists, all accepted conclusions should remain described as dataset-internal measured associations among measured predictors and analysis-defined strata, with biological interpretation, mechanism, causality, single-gene knockout meaning, pathway meaning, clinical meaning, and generalizability remaining unsupported.
